fields.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
fields.note: The fee cap, the two permitted screening processes, the receipt, the return of unused fees, the credit report copy within 7 days, the reusable report provision and the 'not security' rule all appear in the statute text.

fields.quoted_span: The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
fields.note: The $30 base, the CPI adjustment, the itemized receipt, the 7-day credit report copy and the refund timing are all in the statute. The Berkeley Rent Board $68.96 figure for 2026 is not in this document.
The current text, as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, is effective 2026-01-01.

fields.quoted_span: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29.   (AB 1170)   Effective January 1, 2026.)
fields.note: The section is current law as amended. It carries no repeal or sunset language.

fields.quoted_span: “landlord” means an owner of residential rental property.
fields.note: Applicants are defined to include guarantors and cosigners. Subdivision (l) states the section is not intended to preempt federal or state housing assistance program fee rules.
The document is headed Cal. Code CIV 1950.6 and sits in Chapter 2, Hiring of Real Property. AB 1170 and Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 both appear.
